mcq.q: Every profession develops its own _____ to enable its members to communicate effectively with one another.For instance, in the computing field, a“bug”means an error.
From traditional to modern, simple to _____, Christmas tree decorations reflect the personalities of the familiesdecorating the trees.
While reading job seekers’ CVs, employers should be aware that many CVs carry ______ and that some evencontain complete lies.
The teacher was such a ______ person that points were taken off for homework assignments that did notfollow the exact typing format.
The other residents could not understand why Mr. Wang had acted so ______ by constantly trashing theneighborhood.
After joining the weight-losing program, Peter tried very hard to resist the ______ to eat too much dessert.
Because emotional bullying can be the most difficult type of bullying to prove or cope with, its effects canbe ______ and destructive.
To cut down possible sources of _____ when plague threatened, many cities banned the resale of old clothes,which were burned instead.
Jeremy Lin’s improbable success in the NBA prompted a spate of “gee-whiz” stories and added “Linsanity” intoeveryday ______.
The Ghent Altarpiece, widely thought to be one of the most famous panel paintings in the world, has beenadmired and ______ for centuries.
Mike claims to be a rich bachelor, but in fact he is a ______ with two wives living in different cities.
After a decade of impressive growth in Africa, experts believe the year ahead will remain optimistic despite theEurozone crisis and the potential problems it may cause for the continent.
opts: According to the experts, the economic outlook for Africa remains bright.
The year ahead will not look promising unless the Eurozone crisis is solved.
Regardless of the crisis in Africa, the Eurozone stands a good chance to survive.
The continuous growth of Africa has created unknown problems for the Eurozone.

mcq.q: Both the American and the French revolutions developed out of strong convictions about the innate rights ofindividual human beings.
opts: The American revolution broke out because American people strongly believed they had the same inborn rightsas the French.
The French and American revolutions took place because of people’s strong inborn belief that they wereindividuals.
The French revolution broke out because French people firmly believed that they should enjoy the same rights asAmericans.
The American and French revolutions occurred because people firmly believed that each person was naturallyentitled to certain rights.

mcq.q: Artifacts produced in the ancient Egyptian period had a precise role assigned to them in everyday life.
opts: Ancient Egyptians did not separate art from daily life.
Artists were respected and had high social status in ancient Egypt.
Religious art influenced the design of products by ancient Egyptians.
The architecture and decoration of pyramids are the best demonstration of Egyptian art.

mcq.q: Journeys are the midwives of thought.
opts: Great thoughts are generated when you travel.
If you do not take journeys, you cannot be a midwife.
You expand your horizons by traveling with a midwife.

mcq.q: The modern technology has enabled us to split up atoms, but we can’t break down our prejudices.
opts: Nowadays we have been equipped with advanced technology to overcome many extreme challenges, but not toopen our mind.
Scientists need to put in much more effort than what they have put in to split up atoms in order to break downour prejudices.
We will be able to be truly open-minded with the help of the modern technology that has enabled us to splitup atoms.
Advanced technology that has helped us overcome many extreme challenges has made us open-minded.

mcq.q: What are the two major art forms developing within modern history?
mcq.passage: The motion picture is one of two major arts to have evolved within modern history—the other art being still photography, upon which the motion picture is based. (Television is here regarded simply as a means for distribution and exhibition of moving images accompanied by sound.) We can only guess what first prompted people to express themselves in the various older artistic media, or how early modes and conventions developed and disappeared as aesthetic and social functions changed. The motion picture, however, is clearly the child of nineteenth-century scientific curiosity and technological ingenuity; it has grown up under our twentieth-century noses. In fact, the most important of the motion picture’s original reasons for being had nothing to do with its artistic potential. The theory underlying the motion picture was demonstrated in a succession of optical toys. Its tools and materials were invented out of a desire to make visual records of life and to study the movements of animals, including humans. Its capacity to provide peep-show entertainment attracted paying customers to what scientists and inventors had made available. Later, as the novelty of lifelike movement began to pale, the technicians and entrepreneurs who had discovered how to project moving images onto screens stumbled onto an old interest latent in audiences—the story. They began to offer simple narratives in a new form. As in the novel, the play, music, or dance, an ordering of events into a beginning, middle, and end was required in even the simplest motion picture.
